clue.text: Crime writer — one with wicked output

definitions.meaning: Raymond ..., American author of hardboiled detective novels
a ... makes candles, things with wicks, so the output is literally 'wicked'

explanation.surface: A crime novelist whose books are full of evil deeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wicked' looks like 'evil' but is read as 'having a wick': a chandler is a candle-maker.
explanation.definitionFit: Raymond Chandler wrote The Big Sleep; a chandler is also a candle-maker, whose products carry wicks.

clue.text: Make changes to help pair secure operation

indicators.note: make changes to means the letters of help pair are rearranged

parts.note: to cement is to fix or secure

explanation.surface: Adjust things to help a couple seal an agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make changes to' rearranges HELP PAIR into HIP REPLA, and CEMENT follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A hip replacement is a common surgical procedure fitting an artificial joint.

clue.text: Essential items named before marriage (introductions to dating sites)

parts.note: née marks a woman's maiden name, the one she was given before marrying

indicators.note: introductions to picks the opening letter of each of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A guide to what a dating-site user must declare, maiden name included.
explanation.definitionFit: Needs are the necessities, the things one cannot do without.

clue.text: Spill lime and soda over men returning to supply toilets

definitions.note: plural in the clue, but toilets can name a single facility, as the ladies' room is

indicators.note: over means the jumbled letters are spread over and around the next piece
spill means the letters of lime and soda are scattered and rearranged
returning means the soldiers abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers, or men

explanation.surface: Someone knocks over drinks while serving the gents' facilities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spill' mixes LIME SODA into LADIES-OM; 'returning' turns OR into RO, which the mixed letters go over.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladies' room is a women's lavatory in a public building.

clue.text: Stuck-up doctor eating egg I cooked

indicators.note: stuck-up in a down clue means the whole assembly is turned upwards, read in reverse
eating means the doctor abbreviation takes the other letters inside it

explanation.surface: A snooty medic eats an egg that has been prepared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' looks like it describes the egg but is the definition, as in cooked books; 'eating' gives DEGGIR, which 'Stuck-up' turns upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigged means fixed dishonestly, as cooked accounts have been falsified.

clue.text: Flamboyant jumper worn by choice, oddly

indicators.note: the jumper is worn by, i.e. wrapped round, the letters taken from choice

parts.note: a roo, short for kangaroo, is a jumper

indicators.note: oddly means take the odd-numbered letters of the word choice

explanation.surface: A showy sweater someone has picked out to wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' suggests a sweater, which fits 'worn', but it is a kangaroo; the odd letters of 'choice' are C, O, C, which sit inside ROO.
explanation.definitionFit: Rococo is an ornate eighteenth-century style, so the word describes anything showily elaborate.

clue.text: Travel about collecting papers

indicators.note: collecting means the about word gathers the papers inside it

parts.note: re means about, concerning
ID, identity papers

explanation.surface: Someone tours around picking up newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: To ride is to travel on a horse, bike or vehicle.

clue.text: Charlie joins a book club — he should know his way around

definitions.text: he should know his way around

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a driver is a golf club

explanation.surface: A man called Charlie signs up to a reading group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'book club' reads as one thing but splits: B for book and DRIVER, a golf club. London cabbies famously have to learn every street.
explanation.definitionFit: A taxi driver must know the streets thoroughly to take passengers anywhere.

clue.text: Pugilist's complaint about shoulder, essentially — I'm afraid of boxing shame?

parts.note: ca, circa, means about

indicators.note: essentially means the central part of the word shoulder
boxing means the fear phrase encloses the shame word

parts.note: I'm afraid of something means I fear it
to lower someone is to demean or shame them

explanation.surface: A boxer worries about his shoulder and fears losing face in the ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxing' suggests the sport, fitting the pugilist, but it is the containment signal; 'essentially' takes the core of 'shoulder'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cauliflower ear is the swollen, misshapen ear boxers get from repeated blows.

clue.text: Mushroom feast

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to mushroom is to grow and extend rapidly
a lavish meal laid out on a table

explanation.surface: A banquet of fungi.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that mushroom expand outward quickly; a lavish buffet laid out for guests is called a spread.

clue.text: Rover corporation's retaining a lawyer with personal hygiene issue

indicators.note: retaining means the belly word holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: corporation is a jokey word for a pot belly, a gut; the 's stands for 'has'
DA is a district attorney, an American prosecuting lawyer
BO is body odour

explanation.surface: A company employs a lawyer who has body-odour problems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rover' looks like the car brand next to 'corporation', but it means a wanderer; 'corporation' is an old joke word for a paunch.
explanation.definitionFit: A gadabout roams from one social outing to the next, much as a rover wanders.

clue.text: Credit petrol company over bioenergy reserve fund — ultimately, it's inward-looking

parts.note: CR is the standard abbreviation for credit in accounts

indicators.note: over in an across clue means the brand name is turned backwards

parts.note: Esso is a petrol brand

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of each of the three words before it

explanation.surface: A finance story about an oil company's green-energy fund.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses ESSO to OSSE; 'ultimately' takes Y, E, D from the ends of 'bioenergy reserve fund'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cross-eyed eyes both turn in toward the nose, so the gaze is literally directed inward.

clue.text: See 2
How's your father after little brother sent back cycle?

indicators.note: after places the slang phrase's letters behind the reversed brother word
sent back means the short brother word is read backwards

parts.note: bro is a short, informal form of brother
how's your father is British slang for sex, which crosswords also call 'it'

explanation.surface: A cheeky query about Dad after a younger sibling returns a bicycle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'How's your father' is old British slang for sex, which crosswords render as the euphemism 'it'.
explanation.definitionFit: An orbit is one complete circuit round a body, the same as one revolution or cycle.

clue.text: The topless ladies' man turned up with an ecclesiastical scholar

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means the letters read upwards, reversed
topless means the first letter is taken off the top of the word

parts.note: a gigolo is a man paid to keep women company

explanation.surface: A gigolo without his shirt shows up with a churchman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' suggests nudity but removes G from GIGOLO, leaving IGOLO; 'turned up' gives OLOGI.
explanation.definitionFit: A theologian is an expert in religion and doctrine, an academic of the church.

clue.text: Insect breaking in to ferret's food store

indicators.note: breaking in to means the insect goes inside the next word

parts.note: to ferret is to pry or search about; the 's is read as a possessive leading to the definition
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A bug gets into the pet ferret's dinner supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ferret' looks like the animal but is the verb meaning to rummage, PRY.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantry is a small room or cupboard where provisions are kept.

clue.text: Biden regularly on time visiting Conservative after no bad publicity

indicators.note: after puts the party word behind no
visiting means these letters go inside the party word

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

indicators.note: regularly picks alternate letters of the name Biden

explanation.surface: Biden keeps meeting a Tory on schedule, without any bad press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Biden' looks like a news story, but 'regularly' just takes his second and fourth letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Notoriety is fame for something bad, the result of damaging publicity.

clue.text: Swedish on vacation love cycling to clear stuff away

indicators.note: on vacation means the word is emptied of its middle, leaving only its outside letters
cycling means the letters of love are rotated, the first one moving to the end

explanation.surface: A Swede on holiday falls for cycling as a way to tidy up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on vacation' empties Swedish to SH; 'cycling' sends L of LOVE to the back, OVEL.
explanation.definitionFit: To shovel is to scoop up a heap of something and move it out of the way with a spade.

clue.text: First part of play has touching effect

parts.note: Act I is the first part of a play
on can mean touching, as in a hand on a table

explanation.surface: The opening scene of a drama is moving.
explanation.definitionFit: Action is the working or operation of something, so 'come into action' is the same as 'take effect'.

clue.text: Temporarily take refuge — appropriate for all to ring

indicators.note: appropriate here means take one letter for another, so a swap is made in the refuge word

parts.note: a burrow is an animal's refuge underground
U is the British film certificate meaning suitable for all ages
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Someone shelters briefly, and a sanctuary is fitting for everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appropriate' looks like the definition (to borrow is to appropriate) but signals the swap: O, a ring, takes the place of U in BURROW.
explanation.definitionFit: To borrow is to have the use of something for a while before giving it back.

clue.text: Preen Oscar for university ball

indicators.note: Oscar for university means O takes the place of U

parts.note: to doll up is to preen, dressing oneself smartly
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Getting dressed up and winning an award for the university ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ball' looks like a dance, fitting 'preen', but it is a lump.
explanation.definitionFit: A dollop is a shapeless lump of soft food, like a ball of mash.

clue.text: Transport runs on iron railway

indicators.note: on means the runs letter is placed after the iron symbol

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
R is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A train runs on iron rails.
explanation.definitionFit: A ferry is a boat that carries passengers or vehicles across water, a form of transport.

clue.text: Ant 'n' Dec say really good jokes without cracking

indicators.note: cracking means the abbreviation breaks into the jokes word

parts.note: a corker is an excellent example of something, here a great joke
W/O is a written abbreviation for without

explanation.surface: A TV comedy duo tell excellent gags without breaking down laughing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like a link word but is the abbreviation W/O. Ant and Dec are a British TV presenting duo who always appear together.
explanation.definitionFit: Ant and Dec are a long-standing double act, an example of a pair of colleagues working together.

clue.text: Put kilo on, occasionally full of fig pudding

indicators.note: occasionally takes every other letter of full of fig

explanation.surface: Gaining weight from eating a figgy dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Kulfi is an Indian frozen dessert like ice cream, served as a sweet course.

clue.text: Court date leading to deal, maybe

parts.note: to court someone is to woo them

explanation.surface: A romantic date that ends in an agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deal' looks like an agreement but is deal, a softwood timber of pine or fir.
explanation.definitionFit: Deal is a type of timber, an example of wood.

clue.text: Nurse fits in coil, say, rejecting all potential for breeding?

indicators.note: rejecting means the whole assembled string is thrown back, read in the opposite direction
fits in means the nurse letters go between the other two pieces

parts.note: a loop is a coil
say means for example, abbreviated e.g.
EN is an enrolled nurse

explanation.surface: A nurse fitting a contraceptive coil denies any chance of conception.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coil' looks like the contraceptive but means LOOP; 'rejecting' reverses LOOP-EN-EG.
explanation.definitionFit: A gene pool is the total set of inherited variation in a population, all it can pass on by breeding.

clue.text: 2 and 4 expressed as a 12

definitions.note: 12 is REPLACEMENT, so the definition reads 'as a replacement'

parts.note: 2 down starts with HIP, and hip means fashionable, in

indicators.note: expressed means the toilet word is spoken, giving a word that sounds like it

parts.note: 4 down is LADIES ROOM, a toilet, or loo

explanation.surface: A cross-reference puzzle linking three other entries.
explanation.walkthrough: HIP = IN (trendy); the ladies' room is the LOO, said aloud as LIEU.
explanation.definitionFit: In lieu means instead of something, i.e. by way of a substitute.

clue.text: See 8
Suspended journalist on board

indicators.note: on means the journalist abbreviation follows the board word

parts.note: to board somewhere is to stay there as a lodger
ED is an editor, a newspaper journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter is suspended from the company board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' reads as one phrase, as in a director, but splits into an indicator and a synonym for lodge.
explanation.definitionFit: A stayed execution or judgment has been halted for a time, put on hold.

clue.text: Perhaps Shearer offers this nose around German and Italian training for starters

indicators.note: around means the nosy word wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: to nose is to pry
und is German for 'and'

indicators.note: for starters picks the first letter of each of the two words before it

explanation.surface: A TV football pundit nosing into German and Italian training sessions.
explanation.walkthrough: Alan Shearer is a former England footballer who now gives expert comment on TV football coverage.
explanation.definitionFit: Shearer's job on match broadcasts is giving expert opinion, which is what punditry means.
